title: Writing: Academic Discussion: Position
focus: Defender posição sobre pergunta de discussão

content.text: (1 frase) — responda a pergunta do professor.
(1 frase) — mencione um colega (concordando ou discordando).
, não a mesma ideia do colega.
Many universities require students to take courses outside their major. Should these general education requirements be kept, or should students focus only on their main area? Why?
I think they should be kept. Courses in other areas help students think in different ways.
I disagree. University is expensive, and students should spend their time and money on courses that prepare them for their careers.

In my view, general education requirements should be kept. I understand Paulo's concern about cost, but I think he overlooks how much employers value broad skills. Today, most jobs require people to communicate clearly and work with colleagues from other fields, and courses outside your major develop exactly these abilities. For example, my cousin studied engineering, and she says that a required public speaking course was more useful in her first job than some technical classes. So, rather than being a waste of money, these courses are an investment in students' future careers.
(≈ 105 palavras) O aluno lê em voz alta e marca os 4 movimentos.
4.1 Troque e fale: conexão com colegas
they also help us find new interests
→ Paulo / university is expensive / students could take fewer but better courses
→ Maria / creativity / students need more practical skills
Para cada post de colega, crie oralmente um argumento
General education helps students think in different ways.
Students should save money and time.
4.3 Posições rápidas (1 frase de posição + 1 de conexão)
Should first-year students be required to live on campus?
It's too expensive for many families.

content.text: Some people think that cities should ban private cars from their downtown areas to reduce pollution and traffic. Others believe this would hurt local businesses and make life difficult for residents. What do you think? Why?
I support the ban. Cities like Oslo have reduced car traffic in the center, and the air quality improved a lot.
I'm against it. Older people and people with disabilities depend on cars, and public transportation isn't good enough in many cities.

content.text: They help students choose a better major if they discover a new interest.
Students could take these courses online for free if they want.

I partly agree with Kenji, but I think a full ban is too extreme. Laura is right that many people depend on cars, but there is another problem: small shops in the center may lose customers who come from far away. A better solution would be to charge drivers a fee to enter the center and use the money to improve buses. For example, London introduced a congestion charge, and traffic in the center fell while businesses continued to operate. In this way, cities can reduce pollution without excluding anyone.
